name: Heyward-Washington House

dates.altered: The 1930s survey's historical sheet: 'Formerly double verandas adorned the three-story brick structure' (OCR 'Fn~merly couble verandas'). Its data sheet: 'Old kitchen re-stored.'
dates.note: Three dates are on the record because three sources give them: the SC register says 'Built in 1770-71 and acquired by Thomas Heyward, Jr. from his father in 1777'; the 1930s survey sheet prints 'Date of erection: 1750 Builder: Thomas Heyward'; the Wikipedia infobox and the node's exemplar say 1772. Recorded as the state register states it, with the others noted rather than resolved.

refs.title: 2. Historic American Buildings Survey, C.O. Greene, Photographer - Thomas Heyward, Jr. House, 87 Church Street, Charleston, Charleston County, SC
refs.note: The Library titles the item 'Thomas Heyward, Jr. House'; reproduction number HABS SC,10-CHAR,103-. The survey number is read from the data page's own header ('HABS No. SC-64 ... HEYWARD-WASHINGTON HOUSE'). The kitchen building is a separate item, sc0066 (HABS SC,10-CHAR,103A-).
The item id is the path segment of the photo resource the search returned and of the data PDF actually fetched; the landing page itself was not opened. Recorded as `manual` for that reason.

quotes.text: HEYWARD-WASHINGTON HOUSE Charleston, Charleston County, South Carolina Owner: Board of Trustees, Charleston Museum 83 Church Street Date of erection: 1750 -------Builder: Thomas Heyward Present condition: Very good Description: Brick; two and a half stories and basement. Several out-buildings in fair condition. Additional data: Now a museum. Has original furnlture. Old kitchen re-stored. Washington entertained here in 1791.
